title: Secure a ponytail with a plain hair elastic
instruction: Gather the synthetic hair on the practice head into a ponytail and secure it with the plain elastic. Leave it held after both hands let go.
setup: An upright 180 x 156 x 230 mm adult plastic practice head on a 190 mm neck stand and 150 x 150 mm plastic base, with twelve loose 24.5 cm synthetic-hair locks rooted across a 72 mm patch at the back. A separate plain silicone elastic, 30 mm inside diameter, with 3 mm cord thickness, rests on two 6 x 16 x 60 mm wooden rests, 33 mm apart between centres. Both grippers have 40 x 24 x 3 mm silicone-faced steel finger extensions. Nothing joins the locks together or attaches the band to a hand. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 11 of 12 locks pass through the elastic, the band is no wider than 5 cm, and it remains held for three seconds after release. The band must sit at the back of the head, at least 5.5 cm behind its centre and 2.5–16 cm below it. At that position, 0.5 for at least 9 locks or 0.25 for at least 6; otherwise 0. Detached hair or a broken elastic scores 0. Judge the visible locks, band position and released video with a ruler.
fidelity: Flexible lock bundles and a native elastic surface approximate hair and the band. The surface supplies finger contact; rigid patches supply hair/head contact. A native pinch starts in the central 8 mm and holds only the adjacent elastic already enclosed by the real 24 mm faces and releases on opening, 8 mm slip or estimated 6 N tension. Local pinch contacts are filtered while held. The tension estimate is uncalibrated. Hair can bend, escape or snag; no hair or band pose is prescribed.
scores: Dream-1: 0; scripted demo: 1.0. Dream completed across 37 server sessions after expiry recovery.
context: A useful grooming skill combines gathering loose hair with stretching and releasing an elastic around it.
